class_guard: One door per input, one verdict per input, and nothing written before the verdict. (1) remitwatch/door.py: identify(bytes, name) and admit(kind, parsed, context) -> Verdict {decision: read | duplicate | held | refused | not_ours, checks: [{rule, ok, plain reason, dollars}], identity by bytes, content fingerprint, size}. Every path calls it: the server mirror and pending list, the serverless delta and first-load archive, TriZetto, the one-piece upload and the intake pairs, the CLI, zip and gzip members, reports fetched again. Non-file inputs get the same shape: journal entries (a schema per kind), settings (one typed reader with bounds and a safety flag), the state folder (image and ledger hash, size and revision recorded at save and checked at load), owner decisions (require_owner), payer fax numbers. (2) Every reader becomes parse, then check, then apply: only a read verdict reaches the store; a held or refused input writes one verdict row (kind, origin, reasons, dollars it carries, first seen, who decided) and nothing else; supersession and detection never see it. (3) The check list per kind, each rule's false-hold rate measured on a copy of the live store before it holds (0 of 32,696 today for payee, ISA15, dates and trailers): what it is (bytes after a BOM, ST01, workbook or PDF magic; the name breaks ties only); whose (payee TIN and NPI learned from the archive and PRACTICE_TIN, the EMA host, the billing NPI); complete (SE, GE, IEA counts and control numbers, cut-short text, bytes read equal to the listed size); balanced (BPR against claims less PLB: a visible gap in dollars, never superseding a balanced copy); plausible (calendar dates, payment date at most 7 days after its ISA date and the day read, ISA15 = P, amounts that parse, one date order per export); new (content identity for X12 and canonical fields for EMA rows; supersession only between versions with overlapping claims, ranked complete, balanced, claims held, ISA date); size and cost (caps matched to linear parsing; attempts counted per content hash on both hosts, held after two so the cursor moves on). (4) Nothing silent: the Data tab, Today ('3 files held: $4,210 not counted'), the run manifest and the diagnostic bundle list every verdict that is not read, with its reason and dollars; the router's 'skipped' counter, unread problems tables and bare excepts go. (5) Take back: forget(file id) for the owner removes every row an input added, re-runs supersession and detection, and writes before and after counts and dollars to the decision log; a held input can be applied (the owner for ownership and foreign-payee holds) or discarded. (6) The A/R and Production readers (ema_reports, ema_ledger) are the model: their date, money, format, cut-short and shrink holds with Apply and Discard are what the 835 and weekly-export doors adopt.
property_test: Generated door test (release gate 8), both hosts and both store kinds. A generator takes clean invented inputs (835s from tests/test_remitwatch.remit with a correct SE count, exports and reports from tests/ema_fixtures, journal entries, settings) and applies random mutations: a cut at a random byte; a BOM or blank line in front; a renamed ending; another payee's TIN and NPI; ISA15 = T; an amount that cannot be read; an impossible or future date; SE01 off by one; BPR off by one cent to $1,000; the same remittance in a new envelope; a second remittance under the same trace with other claims; a cosmetic column added or removed; a day-first export; another EMA host; a zip or gzip around it; a size past the cap; a journal entry with a bad field or a future time; a setting out of bounds; a missing, older or cut store image. Each input goes through every door (server mirror, serverless delta, TriZetto with tests/fake_sftp, one-piece upload, chunked upload with intake, CLI) in random order. Properties: (a) every input ends with exactly one verdict row a person can see, and none is only 'skipped'; (b) a held or refused input changes nothing else: money totals, transactions, claims, EMA rows, report snapshots, supersession flags and items equal the store without it; (c) the verdict and the resulting store do not depend on the door or the arrival order; (d) reading a clean input again, or its copy under a new name or envelope, changes nothing; (e) forget(file id) after a read returns the store to its earlier state (same items, same dollars) and reading it again restores it; (f) no clean fixture is held, and on a copy of the live store's 835s the ownership, test-flag, date and trailer rules hold nothing (measured today: 0 of 32,696).
